candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record shows elevated β-hydroxybutyrate, persistent anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and glucose levels of 128–142 mg/dL (not markedly elevated), consistent with euglycemic DKA in a diabetic patient post-surgery with inadequate enteral feeding. C001 captures the ketoacidosis and anion-gap components but fails to specify the euglycemic subtype (normal/near-normal glucose distinguishing it from classic DKA) and does not explicitly identify the diabetic etiology, leaving out two required components of the benchmark diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies ketoacidosis with anion-gap but omits the euglycemic qualifier and the diabetic etiology specificity

case_quality_flags: Glucose values reported as 130–160 mmol/L in narrative but 128–142 mg/dL in table — likely a unit transcription error in the narrative; mg/dL values are consistent with euglycemic range and used for diagnosis
Euglycemic DKA precipitated by post-cardiac-surgery starvation state in a diabetic patient on likely SGLT2 inhibitor or insulin-deficient state — precipitant not fully specified in record
